Repackaging certified straight colors into smaller pails for cosmetic customers is permitted under the following conditions: the packaging must prevent changes in composition, be sealed so they cannot be opened without breaking the seal, and any unavoidable change in moisture content due to ordinary exposure during storage, packing, or distribution does not constitute a change in composition. If the packaging material is a food additive, it must be authorized by an appropriate regulation in parts 170 through 189 of this chapter. The term "straight color" includes lakes and substances permitted by specifications for such colors as defined in parts 73, 74, and 81 of this chapter.

21 CFR 70.3(j) [2] defines the term "straight color" to include color additives listed in parts 73, 74, and 81 of this chapter, and such substances as lakes and those permitted by specifications for these colors.

21 CFR 70.20 [1] requires that straight colors be packaged in containers which prevent changes in composition; the packages must be sealed so they cannot be opened without breaking the seal; an unavoidable change in moisture content due to ordinary and customary exposure during good storage, packing, and distribution practice is not considered a change in composition; if the packaging material is a food additive, it shall be authorized by an appropriate regulation in parts 170 through 189 of this chapter.
